title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video and fabricated social media profiles were used to imitate a real, named attorney. The failure sits entirely outside any legitimate AI deployment, as the technology was applied by bad actors rather than misused by a company or institution. The victims encountered the fake personas on mainstream social media platforms, which did not detect or remove the profiles until a third-party anti-piracy service intervened on the attorney's behalf.

The scale, nearly 6,500 profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, shows that platform-level automated detection did not catch the content at volume or speed. The fraud followed a consistent pattern, AI video to establish credibility, WhatsApp for direct contact, fake contracts for legitimacy, and payment apps to collect untraceable funds, indicating a structured operation rather than isolated incidents. That pattern was detectable in principle, but it was a private contractor, not the platforms, that identified and removed the profiles.

What is not established is who is responsible for creating the fraudulent content, where the operation originates, or whether any platform violated its own policies, as those questions are the subject of a planned law enforcement referral and no finding has been made.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of an elaborate artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos impersonating Leal to defraud immigrants, offering services such as US residency assistance for $2,200 cash payments and detainee release services. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office after seeing these fraudulent videos online.

The scams have escalated dramatically in recent months, with Leal's anti-piracy company removing nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms: 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The fraudulent scheme typically directs viewers to contact a WhatsApp number where scammers send fake contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App. Leal plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the origin of the scams and is warning immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online.
